transcript.text: Good morning everyone. We're here for the readiness review on the real-time collaboration service ahead of Monday's 09:00 UTC production launch. The service passed its staging tests — functional, failover, and basic load — and we have the draft launch plan in front of us. Before I finalize and record the binding policy, I want to give each of you a chance to raise any final concerns. Let's go through it systematically: backend engineering, reliability, privacy, and customer success. Who'd like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to raise a concern before we finalize. While investigating an unrelated mobile performance report this afternoon, I confirmed that mobile clients resume from background in bursts and currently retry every 5 seconds, which can create a reconnect storm. The draft launch plan uses the client library's default 5-second retry interval, but I believe the rollout policy should set the retry interval to exactly 30 seconds to mitigate this risk. I have not yet filed the client-library ticket for this.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a capacity concern. About 20 minutes ago I completed a production-traffic replay and confirmed that the collaboration cluster's safe connection ceiling for Monday is exactly 6,000 concurrent connections — not the 10,000 in the draft plan. The autoscaling limit hasn't been updated yet because I'm still attaching the replay results to the capacity worksheet, but the data is solid. We need to lower the concurrent connection cap to 6,000 before finalizing.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to raise a privacy concern before we finalize. I completed a privacy review this morning and confirmed two requirements that conflict with the draft launch plan. First, collaboration content for EU accounts must remain in the EU processing region — the draft plan stores all collaboration data in the primary production region, which would not satisfy this. Second, session transcripts must be deleted after exactly 30 days, not the 90 days in the draft plan. I haven't opened the compliance ticket yet because legal was still reviewing the wording, but these are binding requirements that need to be reflected in the launch policy before we finalize.

transcript.text: I need to raise a customer success concern before we finalize. I reconciled the customer-success rollout spreadsheet an hour ago and confirmed that six accounts — acct-204, acct-219, acct-233, acct-241, acct-278, and acct-301 — have administrator opt-out commitments until their enablement sessions are complete. These six accounts must be excluded from Monday's 10% rollout. I have not updated the launch checklist yet, so we need to make sure this exclusion is captured in the binding policy before we finalize.
